subtitle: Midterm Important MCQs
topics: Operating System Basics and System Calls

mcqs.topic: Operating System Basics and System Calls
mcqs.question: The two main functions of an operating system are to provide the user with an extended (virtual) machine and to:
options: Manage the I/O devices and other system resources
Compile user programs into machine code
Connect the computer to the Internet

mcqs.topic: Operating System Basics and System Calls
mcqs.question: System calls provide the interface between:
options: A process and the operating system
The user and the command interpreter

mcqs.topic: Operating System Basics and System Calls
mcqs.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the main types of system calls?

mcqs.topic: Operating System Basics and System Calls
mcqs.question: In the top-down view of an operating system, all services are involved and accomplished through ______ calls.

mcqs.topic: Operating System Basics and System Calls
mcqs.question: A trap is caused by ______ and is synchronous.
options: An event external to the processor

mcqs.topic: Operating System Basics and System Calls
mcqs.question: Which of the following operations may safely be performed in user mode?

mcqs.topic: Operating System Basics and System Calls
mcqs.question: Multiprogramming keeps the CPU busy mainly by:
options: Running several programs on several processors
Switching the CPU to another process while one process waits for I/O
Increasing the clock speed of the CPU

mcqs.topic: Operating System Basics and System Calls
mcqs.question: Spooling uses ______ as a huge buffer for holding output for devices such as printers.

mcqs.topic: Operating System Basics and System Calls
mcqs.question: On early computers there was no DMA, so every byte of data read or written was handled by the CPU. The main implication of this was that:
options: The CPU remained fully occupied doing I/O, so multiprogramming gained little in CPU utilization
The operating system had to be written in assembly language

mcqs.topic: Operating System Basics and System Calls
mcqs.question: The main purpose of having two distinct modes, kernel mode and user mode, is to:
options: Protect the operating system from erroneous or malicious user programs
Allow more than one user to log in
Reduce the size of the kernel

mcqs.topic: Operating System Basics and System Calls
mcqs.question: The command interpreter is usually kept separate from the kernel because:
options: It runs faster outside the kernel
It is not needed for the kernel's working and can be changed or replaced without modifying the kernel
The kernel cannot read user commands
It must be written in a different language

mcqs.topic: Operating System Basics and System Calls
mcqs.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the five major activities of an operating system in regard to process management?
options: Provision of mechanisms for process synchronization

mcqs.question: In a microkernel-based system, policy decisions are made in user space, while the mechanisms are implemented in:
In ______ architecture of process assignment, key kernel functions always run on a particular processor.
In ______ architecture of process assignment, the operating system can execute on any processor and each processor does its own self-scheduling.
A non-process kernel executes the kernel code outside of any ______.
The primary disadvantage of the microkernel architecture is:
options: It is less secure than a monolithic kernel
The overhead of inter-process communication and message passing between user processes and system services
New services cannot be added to it

mcqs.question: An important benefit of the microkernel architecture is that:
options: Adding a new service does not require modifying the kernel
It eliminates the need for system calls
It makes device drivers run in kernel mode

mcqs.question: Separating policy from mechanism in a microkernel-based operating system means that:
options: All policies are fixed inside the kernel
Basic mechanisms are implemented in the kernel while policy decisions are made by user-level servers
User programs make all mechanism decisions
The kernel contains no mechanisms at all

mcqs.question: Load sharing in a multiprocessor system refers to making sure that:
options: All processes share a single address space
No processor sits idle while other processors have waiting processes
All processors run at the same clock speed
Processes are never migrated between processors

mcqs.question: A progress graph is used to depict:
options: The memory layout of a process
The discrete execution state space of concurrent threads

mcqs.question: If a parent process terminates without reaping its child, the child process will be reaped by the ______ process.
Explicit reaping is only required for ______ running processes.
The fork() system call returns ______ in the child process.
A process that has terminated but whose parent has not yet reaped it is called a:
All threads belonging to the same process share:
options: The process address space, including code, data and heap

mcqs.question: A thread may fail to be created when:
options: The process already has one thread
The system has reached its limit on the number of threads or has insufficient resources such as memory

mcqs.question: A multithreaded solution on a single-processor system performs better than a single-threaded solution when:
options: A thread frequently blocks, for example on a page fault, so another thread can use the CPU in the meantime
The program uses no shared data
There is only one kernel thread

mcqs.question: A function is called ______ if and only if it accesses no shared variables when called from multiple threads.
User ______ can create lots of kernel work, i.e. many network packets may come in that the operating system has to process when doing a read or write system call.
In the fork_test() code discussed in lectures, five new processes are created in total (excluding the calling process). The final printf("Whatsup") line is therefore printed:
Threads are considered harmful mainly because:
options: Synchronization bugs such as race conditions and deadlocks are easy to introduce and very hard to find and fix

mcqs.question: The process table is needed in a timesharing system in order to:
options: Store the files of all users
Keep track of the state of every process so that a preempted process can be restarted later

mcqs.question: A queue of threads waiting for something inside a critical region is called a:
If two threads are waiting for a lock and both see it ______, only one of them will grab it.
A semaphore is a variable that is manipulated atomically through the two operations:
When a semaphore is used for mutual exclusion, its initial value is:
options: Equal to the number of threads

mcqs.question: Condition variables support exactly three operations, which are:
Condition variables are not cumulative, which is why they must be used together with a:
Because condition variables are not cumulative, a signal that is sent when no thread is waiting is:
options: Stored for the next waiting thread
Lost, because signals are not remembered

mcqs.question: The lost wakeup problem in condition-variable implementations can be resolved by:
options: The deferred signal approach or the speculative signal approach
Using a larger number of locks

mcqs.question: In a monitor, at any one moment:
options: Many processes may execute monitor procedures simultaneously
Only one process may be active inside the monitor
No process may wait inside the monitor

mcqs.question: In the readers/writers problem, the access rules are that:
options: Many readers and many writers may access the data together
Many readers may read at the same time, but a writer must have exclusive access
Only one reader may read at a time
Writers always have priority over readers

mcqs.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the classical synchronization problems?
A race condition occurs when:
options: The outcome of a program depends on the order in which threads execute
A thread waits too long for a lock
The CPU runs out of work

mcqs.question: A thread that returns from a wait on a condition variable must test the condition expression again before proceeding, because:
options: The signal operation erases the condition
Returning from wait is only a hint that the condition may have become true; another thread may have changed the state first
Condition variables always wake up all threads
The lock is never released during a wait

mcqs.question: ______ scheduling assigns priorities to tasks on the basis of their periods.
In rate-monotonic scheduling, priorities are assigned so that a task with a shorter period gets:
options: The same priority as all other tasks

mcqs.question: The rate-monotonic scheduling algorithm uses:
The STCF (Shortest Time to Completion First) scheduler runs the job that:
options: Has the least amount of work left to do

mcqs.question: In SCHED_FIFO scheduling, once a thread starts running it continues to run until it:
options: Is preempted by any newly ready thread
Blocks or voluntarily yields the CPU

mcqs.question: Which of the following scheduling algorithms is non-preemptive?
In preemptive scheduling, the operating system:
options: Can suspend a running process and give the CPU to another process
Is used only in batch systems

mcqs.question: Putting two pointers to the same PCB in the ready queue of a round-robin scheduler effectively:
options: Decreases the priority of that process
Gives that process CPU time more often, i.e. preferential (higher priority) treatment
Doubles the memory of the process

mcqs.question: Interrupts are caused by events ______ to the processor.
In priority scheduling, low-priority processes may wait indefinitely. This problem is called ______ and is commonly solved by aging.
Which of the following is NOT one of the four necessary conditions for deadlock?
Preventing deadlock by imposing a total ordering on all resources and requiring requests in increasing order ensures that ______ never occurs.
If a system is in an unsafe state, then:
options: Deadlock is possible, but the processes may still complete their execution without entering a deadlock
The operating system must be restarted

mcqs.question: Three processes share 4 resources of the same type and every process needs at most 2 resources. The system is guaranteed to be deadlock-free because:
options: At least one process can always obtain both resources it needs, complete, and release them
Each process holds exactly one resource

mcqs.question: In a resource allocation graph with single-instance resources, a cycle in the graph indicates that:
options: The system is in a safe state
A deadlock exists among the processes in the cycle

mcqs.question: Deadlock prevention works by ensuring that:
options: At least one of the four necessary conditions for deadlock can never hold
The system never enters a safe state

mcqs.question: In ______ allocation, the application explicitly allocates and frees memory space.
______ fragmentation occurs when there is enough total heap memory available, but no single free block is large enough to satisfy a request.
Internal fragmentation is the wasted space that occurs:
options: Inside an allocated block, because the block is larger than the requested payload
When the heap is completely full

mcqs.question: In an implicit free list, the allocator finds a free block by:
options: Following pointers stored in free blocks
Scanning the blocks of the heap one by one using the size in each block's header
Asking the operating system for each request
Using a hash table of block sizes

mcqs.question: In an explicit free list, the doubly linked list contains:
options: Only blocks larger than a fixed size

mcqs.question: The worst-case allocation time of an implicit free list is proportional to:
options: The number of free blocks only
The total number of blocks in the heap
The size of the largest block

mcqs.question: With simple segregated free lists (without coalescing while freeing), freeing a block takes:
options: Time proportional to the heap size
Constant time, because the block is simply placed on the list for its size class
Time proportional to the number of free blocks
Time proportional to the block size

mcqs.question: Coalescing in dynamic memory allocation means:
options: Splitting a free block into two smaller blocks
Merging adjacent free blocks into one larger free block
Copying a block to a new location

mcqs.question: In the boundary-tag method, each block carries a header and a footer so that the allocator can:
options: Find and merge with the previous free block when a block is freed

mcqs.question: With a 4-byte header, a 4-byte footer, double-word (8-byte) alignment and no zero-size payloads allowed, the minimum block size is:
In a block header word, the allocation status (allocated or free) is usually stored in:
options: The least significant bit(s) of the size word
